{{short description|American logician (1908–1987)}}
{{infobox academic|birth_date=September 9, 1908|birth_place=[[Greenwich, Connecticut]], US|death_date=September 18, 1987|death_place=[[New Haven, Connecticut]], US |discipline=[[Logic]]|alma_mater=[[Yale University]]|known_for=[[Fitch's paradox of knowability]]}}

'''Frederic Brenton Fitch''' (September 9, 1908 – September 18, 1987) was an American [[logician]], a [[Sterling Professor]] at [[Yale University]].<ref>{{citation|title=Frederic B. Fitch|date=September 19, 1987|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|department=Obituaries|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/09/19/obituaries/frederic-b-fitch.html}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
At Yale, Fitch earned his B.A in 1931 and his Ph.D. in 1934 under the supervision of [[F. S. C. Northrop]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=106324}}</ref> From 1934 to 1937 Fitch was a postdoc at the [[University of Virginia]]. In 1937 he returned to Yale, where he taught until his retirement in 1977.<ref name="Shook2005">{{cite book |author=Anellis, Irving H. |title=[[Dictionary of Modern American Philosophers]] |date=1 January 2005 |publisher=A&C Black |isbn=978-1-84371-037-0 |editor=Shook, John R. |pages=799–802 |chapter=Fitch, Frederic Brenton |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ijpj1tB3Qr0C&pg=PA799 |authorlink=Irving Anellis}}</ref>

His doctoral students include [[Alan Ross Anderson]], [[Ruth Barcan Marcus]], and [[William W. Tait]].

==Work==
Fitch was the [[inventor]] of the [[Fitch notation]] for arranging formal logical proofs as diagrams.<ref>{{citation|title=Proof Theory: Sequent Calculi and Related Formalisms|series=Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications|first=Katalin|last=Bimbó|author-link= Katalin Bimbó |publisher=CRC Press|year=2014|isbn=9781466564688|page=272|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ulzOBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA272}}.</ref> In his 1963 published paper "A Logical Analysis of Some Value Concepts" he proves "Theorem 5" (originally by [[Alonzo Church]]), which later became famous in context of the [[Fitch's paradox of knowability|knowability paradox]].<ref>{{Cite SEP|url-id=fitch-paradox|title=Fitch's Paradox of Knowability|author-last1=Brogaard|author-first1=Berit|author-link1=Berit Brogaard|author-last2=Salerno|author-first2=Joe|author-link2=|date=Fall 2019}}</ref>

Fitch worked primarily in [[combinatory logic]], authoring an undergraduate-level textbook on the subject (1974), but he also made significant contributions to [[intuitionism]] and [[modal logic]]. He was interested in the problem of the consistency, completeness, categoricity, and constructivity of logical theories, especially [[Non-classical logic|non-classical logics]], and contributed to the [[foundations of mathematics]] and to [[inductive probability]]. He dealt with the [[Theory of reference|theory of references]] in "The Problem of the Morning Star and the Evening Star" (1949).<ref name="Shook2005"/>

He also contributed to the philosophy of how logic relates to language.<ref name="Shook2005"/>

==Works==
* 1952: ''[[iarchive:symboliclogicint0000fitc|Symbolic Logic, An Introduction]]'', The Ronald Press Company<ref name="TurquetteFitch1953">{{cite journal|last1=Turquette|first1=Atwell R.|title=Review of ''Symbolic Logic: An Introduction'' by Frederich Brenton Fitch|journal=[[The Philosophical Review]]|volume=62|issue=4|year=1953|pages=617–619|issn=0031-8108|doi=10.2307/2182470|jstor=2182470 }}</ref>
* 1963: [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2271594 "A Logical Analysis of Some Value Concepts"], {{doi|10.2307/2271594}} (This paper has over 400 citations.)
* 1974: ''[[iarchive:elementsofcombin0000fitc|Elements of Combinatory Logic]]'', [[Yale University Press]]<ref name="Lercher2014">{{cite journal|last1=Lercher|first1=Bruce|title=Review of ''Elements of Combinatory Logic''|journal=[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]]|volume=41|issue=4|year=2014|pages=789–790|issn=0022-4812|doi=10.2307/2272401|jstor=2272401 |s2cid=60486915 }}</ref>
* 1975: (with [[Alan Ross Anderson]], [[Ruth Barcan Marcus]], and [[Richard Milton Martin]]): {{cite book |title=The Logical Enterprise |date=1975 |publisher=[[Yale University Press]] |isbn=978-0-300-01790-8 |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/logicalenterpris0000unse}}
